title: 秋夜将晓出篱门迎凉有感·其二
titlePy: Qiū Yè Jiāng Xiǎo Chū Lí Mén Yíng Liáng Yǒu Gǎn
titleEn: Stepping Out of My Gate Before Dawn on an Autumn Night (No. 2)
author: 陆游
intro: The Yellow River and Mount Hua, grand as ever — but they lie in enemy hands. The people left behind in the north weep, looking south year after year for an army that never comes.
analysis: 这首诗写于1192年秋天，陆游六十八岁，住在山阴。一个闷热的秋夜，天快亮时他走出篱笆门乘凉，想到被金人占领的北方。前两句写北方的山河：三万里长的黄河向东流入大海，五千仞高的华山直上云天。“三万里”“五千仞”都是夸张，写出祖国山河的雄伟。可是这么壮丽的山河却在敌人手里。后两句写北方的百姓：他们在金人的统治下眼泪都流干了，一年又一年向南方盼望，等着宋朝的军队来收复，却一次次落空。“又一年”三个字很沉重，写出了漫长的等待和失望。诗没有直接批评朝廷，但读者能感到作者的愤怒和悲哀：前面的山河越壮美，后面的遗民就越可怜。
analysisEn: Lu You wrote this in the autumn of 1192, aged sixty-seven, at home in Shanyin. On a hot autumn night he stepped out of his garden gate before dawn to cool off, and his thoughts went north, to the land held by the Jin. The first two lines show that land at its grandest: the Yellow River, thirty thousand lǐ long, flowing east into the sea; Mount Hua, five thousand rèn high, rubbing against the sky. Both numbers are deliberate exaggerations — they make the mountains and rivers of the homeland feel immense. But this magnificent country is in enemy hands. The second couplet turns to the people. The Chinese left behind under Jin rule have cried until there are no tears left in the “barbarian dust”, and they look south, year after year, for the imperial army to come and free them — and again it does not come. The phrase 又一年 (“another year”) carries all that waiting and disappointment. Lu You never attacks the court by name, yet the anger is clear: the grander the land in the first half, the more pitiful the people in the second. It is the second of two poems with this title.
background: Lu You (1125–1210) spent his life urging the Southern Song to win back northern China, lost to the Jin in 1127. He wrote this pair of poems in the autumn of 1192, in retirement at Shanyin.
pronunciation: 将晓 jiāng；仞 rèn（古代长度单位）；遗民 yí。
version: 采用通行教材文本（统编教材五年级下册）。原作共两首，这是第二首。

lines.py: sān wàn lǐ hé dōng rù hǎi
lines.lit: The thirty-thousand-li river flows east into the sea;
lines.en: The Yellow River runs thirty thousand miles east to the sea;

lines.py: wǔ qiān rèn yuè shàng mó tiān
lines.lit: the five-thousand-ren mountain rises to rub the sky.
lines.en: Mount Hua climbs five thousand fathoms to brush the sky.

lines.py: yí mín lèi jìn hú chén lǐ
lines.lit: The left-behind people’s tears are used up in the invaders’ dust;
lines.en: Under the invaders’ dust, the people left behind have no tears left;

lines.py: nán wàng wáng shī yòu yī nián
lines.lit: looking south for the royal army — another year.
lines.en: they look south for the emperor’s army — another year goes by.

words.note: 将：快要，现代汉语“即将”；晓：天亮。

words.en: a gate in a bamboo fence

words.note: 古汉语里“河”常专指黄河，“江”专指长江；今天泛指一切河流。

words.en: an ancient unit of height (about 2 metres)

words.note: 现代汉语“五岳”指五座名山。
现代汉语“摩天大楼”“摩天轮”。

words.en: people left behind under foreign rule
dust raised by the invaders — enemy rule
words.note: 胡：古代对北方民族的称呼，今天“胡萝卜”“胡琴”里还有。
师：军队，现代汉语“师长”“出师”。

imagery.name: 黄河
imagery.zh: 奔流入海的黄河写出北方山河的壮阔，也让人痛惜它落入敌手。
imagery.en: The Yellow River pouring into the sea shows how grand the north is — and how painful its loss.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 高耸入云的华山是祖国山河雄伟的象征。
imagery.en: Mount Hua towering into the clouds stands for the majesty of the homeland.

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: “泪尽”写北方百姓长期受苦、哭干眼泪，盼望已到极点。
imagery.en: “Tears used up”: northern people who have suffered so long they have nothing left but hope.
